About

I'm a mechanical engineer working full time as a process engineer at Matcor Metal Fabrication in Brampton. I joined as a co-op student in September 2024 and stayed on. Day to day that means nesting parts for high yield, running time studies on production workflows, and designing process changes and Kaizen improvements that raise plant efficiency.

I earned my B.Eng. from York University in 2025. Alongside coursework and work I keep building: mechanism design and kinematics, CFD and FEA studies, and hardware projects that combine CAD, Arduino, and code. I like taking a system apart, in CAD or otherwise, to see why it behaves the way it does.

Outside of engineering, I sketch, paint, and sculpt. The process is nearly identical: plan carefully, adapt when something doesn't go to plan, and stay patient with the details until the whole thing holds together.

How I Approach Engineering

Creativity, lifelong learning, and problem-solving are the three ideals I design around — they're what pulled me toward mechanical engineering in the first place, and what I think lets an engineer see a problem that others miss.

I want to keep building fluency outside my own discipline too — the business, marketing, and manufacturing sides of a product — so I can work every station of the process, not just one, and help a design actually reach the people it's meant for.
